content.text: Now I understand the structure. This is a Next.js 16 app using the App Router. I'll create a middleware file to log every request to the console. In Next.js, middleware is the best approach for logging all requests.

Perfect! I've added request logging to your Next.js app by creating a middleware file at `/vercel/sandbox/middleware.ts`. 

This middleware will:

1. Log every incoming request with:
   - Timestamp in ISO format
   - HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
   - Full URL
   - User-Agent header

2. The matcher configuration excludes Next.js internal routes like:
   - `_next/static` (static files)
   - `_next/image` (image optimization)
   - `favicon.ico`

When you run the app with `npm run dev` and visit any page, you'll see console output like:

```
[2026-02-05T20:36:00.000Z] GET http://localhost:3000/
  User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 ...
```

The middleware intercepts all requests and then passes them through with `NextResponse.next()` so your app continues to work normally.
